title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 9: a great light in Galilee, the child born to us and his names, and the hand stretched out still.

questions.text: Which lands were brought into contempt in the former time?
questions.explanation: In the former time he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the latter time he has made it glorious.

questions.text: What have the people who walked in darkness seen?
questions.explanation: The text says, "The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light."

questions.text: As in which day has the rod of the oppressor been broken?
questions.explanation: The yoke of his burden, the staff of his shoulder, and the rod of his oppressor have been broken as in the day of Midian.

questions.text: Where will the government be, for the child who is born to us?
questions.explanation: The text says, "For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders."

questions.text: Which of these is one of the names the child will be called?
questions.explanation: His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

questions.text: On whose throne will his government and peace be established?
questions.explanation: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David's throne and on his kingdom.

questions.text: What do the proud inhabitants of Samaria say they will build with after the bricks have fallen?
questions.explanation: In pride they say, "The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."

questions.text: Who is the tail that Yahweh will cut off from Israel?
questions.explanation: The text explains, "The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail."

questions.text: Like what does wickedness burn, devouring the briers and thorns?
questions.explanation: The text says, "For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest."

questions.text: Which refrain closes this chapter after Manasseh and Ephraim turn against Judah?
questions.explanation: The chapter ends, "For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still."

answers.text: "And there was peace in the land"
"For the mouth of Yahweh has spoken it"
